messages:
sam: Hey — seeing a flaky SSE stream in the Go SDK when the auth token refresh kicks in. The client sometimes logs a 401 during the initial handshake, then we get torn/partial JSON events and the goroutine reading the stream ends up blocked on writes to a buffered channel. Anyone seen this pattern?

lina: Can you paste the minimal client code + the log snippet? Is this only when token refresh overlaps the initial connect or also during long-lived streams? :thinking:

sam: Minimal repro attached inline:
```go
req, _ := http.NewRequest("GET", url, nil)
req.Header.Set("Accept", "text/event-stream")
req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer " + token)
resp, _ := client.Do(req)
scanner := bufio.NewScanner(resp.Body)
for scanner.Scan() {
  line := scanner.Text()
  // naive: assume each data: line is a full JSON chunk
  // send to parseCh <- line
}
```
Logs: `sse: handshake failed 401`, then `parse: unexpected EOF` and later `worker stuck writing to parseCh (buffer full)`

pranav: Two things probably interacting: 1) auth handshake race where the server rejects the initial request while token refresh runs, causing the client to get a truncated response; 2) the parser assumes whole JSON objects per SSE data line. In practice the server may stream partial fragments that need reassembly.

pranav: Fixes I'd try: (a) Make the handshake idempotent + retry on 401 with backoff before starting the stream read loop. (b) Replace Scanner with incremental reader + accumulator that only attempts json.Unmarshal when you have a complete object. (c) Use a bounded semaphore for parse queue and drop/metrics when the queue is full instead of blocking writers.

lina: Example incremental logic we used recently (pseudo):
```go
var buf bytes.Buffer
dec := json.NewDecoder(&buf)
for {
  chunk := readSSEDataChunk() // may be partial JSON fragment
  buf.Write(chunk)
  for {
    var obj map["string"]any
    if err := dec.Decode(&obj); err == io.EOF || err == io.ErrUnexpectedEOF {
      break // need more bytes
    } else if err != nil {
      // handle parse error (log + drop)
      buf.Reset()
      break
    }
    // process obj
  }
}
```
This avoids assuming newline-delimited JSON.

sam: Nice. Regarding the auth retry — do we retry transparently inside the SDK or expose a hook so apps can coordinate token refresh? The current SDK refresh is async and updates a shared token provider; race window is about ~200ms.

pranav: I argued earlier we should do a short, deterministic handshake retry inside the SDK: on 401 during initial GET, try one token-refresh-and-retry with jittered sleep up to 150ms, then give up and bubble error. That keeps apps simpler. Also set req.Header "Accept: text/event-stream" explicitly and use the same http.Client across retries to reuse connections.

lina: Also look at Transport settings. We had a case where DisableKeepAlives=false and KeepAlive timeouts caused half-open sockets while refresh happened. For the client we set: `Transport{MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 100, IdleConnTimeout: 30s}` and used `Request.WithContext(ctx)` so cancellation during token refresh aborts in-flight requests.

sam: For the backpressure I was using a buffered channel parseCh size 64 and a pool of 4 parser goroutines. When parseCh is full the producer goroutine blocks and eventually server keeps sending and memory balloons. How to safely signal upstream to slow down?

pranav: Server-side you can't control push rate. Two options: (1) If you control the SDK reader, enforce a small in-memory window and when full switch to dropping non-essential events + emit a metrics counter. (2) Apply a bounded worker + semaphore and return quickly from the reader path with a simple ack to the caller to signal overflow. In Go SDK we prefer option (1) + a simple backpressure metric and a user-configurable drop policy (oldest/newest).

lina: Another trick — have the reader block on disk-backed queue (tmp file) instead of memory when the buffer is full. It keeps your memory small but increases latency for downstream processing. Worth it for long-lived misbehaving streams.

sam: Great suggestions. I'll prototype: add handshake-retry (1 retry), switch to incremental json.Decoder with bytes.Buffer, and change parse queue to bounded with drop-oldest policy + metric. I'll share a small PR to devex next hour. :thumbsup:

devex-bot: Reminder: if you add retry logic, include a flag in the SDK config so customers in gated environments can disable it (cc @security).

pranav: Agreed. Also add an integration test that simulates auth-refresh during connect and a test that streams deliberately split JSON fragments across SSE events. Helps prevent regressions.

sam: Will do — thanks all.
